one_liner: Racket Brainfuck runner that turns the program into Racket syntax and evals it; 1.24x faster than kostya's C++ interpreter on bench.b only.
what_it_does: brainfuck/bf-staged.rkt (114 lines, by philnguyen in PR #296, February 2021, tuned in PR #300 and renamed from bf-syntax.rkt in PR #462) parses a Brainfuck program straight into a Racket syntax object, wraps it in a lambda over the tape vector, position and printer, and calls eval on it. The resulting procedure is the program. It is a benchmark program, not a library: there is no API beyond parse and run, and only the suite's Brainfuck subset is handled (',' input is ignored).
how_it_is_fast: This is a hand-staged interpreter (a first Futamura projection done with Racket's macro-time syntax objects): each '+', '-', '<', '>' and '.' becomes a call to a small local helper (tape-inc!, tape-move, tape-print) nested around the previous expression, and each '[' becomes a named-let loop whose else branch holds the rest of the program. Under Racket CS, eval hands that form to the Chez Scheme compiler, so the program runs as native code with no instruction fetch, switch or op-vector walk, which is all the C++ baseline does per instruction. The generated code reads and writes the tape with unsafe-vector*-ref/set! and adds with unsafe-fx+ (imported under the safe names). PLT_CS_COMPILE_LIMIT=100000 in common/commands.mk keeps larger generated forms in machine-code mode instead of Racket CS's interpreter fallback.
when_to_use: As a pattern for Racket DSLs: an embedded rule, filter or bytecode language known only at run time whose programs run long enough to amortise one eval (bench.b: 172 instructions, 0.885 s total).
Small programs dominated by tight nested loops: bench.b is 172 instructions with loops nested eight deep, ending in a [-] clear loop, the shape where compiling away dispatch pays most.
When you already ship Racket CS and want interpreter-to-native speedups without writing a compiler back end: the code generator is a 16-line match over characters.
Comparing staging techniques across runtimes: the same table holds C# (Staged) and Scala (Staged) versions of the identical task.
when_not_to_use: As evidence that Racket beats C++ at equal work: the same-algorithm Racket interpreter (bf.rkt) takes 1.761 s on bench.b and 35.373 s on mandel.b against C++/g++ 1.097 s and 10.143 s, and no C++ staged or JIT variant was measured.

Large programs: on mandel.b (10,765 instructions) the staged version takes 15.722 s, 1.55x slower than C++/g++ and slower than the plain Rust (14.460 s) and C# (15.576 s) interpreters, with a 71.69 MiB RSS increase against 2.75 MiB for plain Racket.
Memory- or start-up-sensitive processes: 101.37 MiB base RSS against 3.38 MiB for the C++ interpreter, before any code is generated.
Untrusted programs: the generated code uses unsafe vector and fixnum operations, so a program that moves left of cell 0 reads and writes outside the vector instead of raising an error.
Racket BC or deployments that cannot set PLT_CS_COMPILE_LIMIT: the measured configuration depends on Racket CS's machine-code mode and that environment variable for mid-sized programs.

integration.form: source-drop (one Racket module, brainfuck/bf-staged.rkt, run with racket and no raco make step)
integration.dependencies: Racket base libraries only: racket/file, racket/list, racket/match, racket/cmdline, racket/os, racket/tcp (for the suite's notify hook) and racket/unsafe/ops
integration.min_toolchain: Racket CS; measured with Racket 9.2 (x86_64 linux-cs installer per docker/Dockerfile) and PLT_CS_COMPILE_LIMIT=100000; older versions not documented
integration.platforms: any platform Racket CS supports; measured on x86-64 Linux (Intel Xeon E-2324G) only
integration.thread_safety: not documented; each run builds its own tape vector and the printer is a mutable struct passed in, so concurrent runs would need separate printers

gotchas: Different algorithm from the baseline, accepted by the suite with mixed signals: owner kostya approved PR #296 on 2021-02-24 with 'seems ok, because it still interpret every instruction one by one', while collaborator nuald wrote in issue #485 (2024-03-20) that staged variants are 'not the reference implementations, and rather included just for testing purposes'. Under Racket CS the eval'd lambda is compiled to Chez machine code, not interpreted, and brainfuck/README.md asks every implementation to interpret instructions one by one.

PLT_CS_COMPILE_LIMIT=100000 was added suite-wide in PR #301 (2021-03-04, no rationale given). Racket CS interprets the outer layer of any linklet larger than the limit (default 10000; racket/src/cs/linklet.sls) and compiles only smaller inner lambdas. Counting the instruction mix with schemify's size rules (an estimate, not measured) gives about 430 terms for bench.b and about 26,000 for mandel.b, so the bench.b result does not depend on the variable but the mandel.b result does.

The tape grows only on the right: tape-move checks the upper bound, and the reads and writes are unsafe-vector*-ref/set!, so a negative position silently corrupts memory (the C++ size_t index is undefined behaviour there too). The module's (#%declare #:unsafe) covers the module itself; inside the generated code only the renamed primitives are unsafe, and '>' in the loop test stays the generic racket/base comparison.

The timed region (between the notify calls) includes parsing, syntax construction and the Chez compile of the generated form, but verify() runs one staged eval of a Hello World program before timing, so expander and compiler warm-up is excluded; .NET, JVM and Racket start-up are outside the timer for every language.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Only when your host language is Racket: C# (Staged) runs bench.b in 0.373 s with 36.6 MiB and Scala (Staged) in 0.409 s with 229.6 MiB against 0.885 s here, and both also beat C++ on mandel.b where this entry loses. If you must stay in C++, the catalogued ClangJIT and Proteus entries give the same run-time specialisation through LLVM.
verified_claims_summary: kostya/benchmarks (README update 2026-07-19, Intel Xeon E-2324G, Debian forky/sid Docker image, median of 10 quiet runs with MAD) shows the staged Racket 9.2 CS runner at 0.885 s and 34.39 J on bench.b against 1.097 s and 46.21 J for the C++ AST interpreter built with g++ 16.1.0 -O3 -march=native -flto=auto (C/gcc 1.112 s, C++/clang++ 22.1.8 with libc++ 1.167 s), about 1.24x (derived from page data). It is run-time compilation of the Brainfuck program set against an interpreter, and it reverses on mandel.b (15.722 s against 10.143 s).
status_note: The suite is active and MIT-licensed (README update 2026-07-19); bf-staged.rkt has not changed since its 2023 rename and is a copyable 114-line teaching sample of Racket staging rather than a maintained library.
